Egyptian agriculture was revolutionary for its time, characterized by the annual inundation of the Nile River, which deposited rich, nutrient-dense silt that transformed desert into fertile land. Egyptian agriculture was revolutionary for its time, characterized by the annual inundation of the Nile River, which deposited rich, nutrient-dense silt that transformed desert into fertile land.
